cohort: Patients who underwent cesarean delivery at a single tertiary center
finding: The use of knotless barbed sutures for uterine and subcuticular closure during cesarean delivery was associated with lower white blood cell counts on postoperative day 1 compared to monofilament sutures, with no other significant differences in short-term outcomes.
mod_finding: The study investigated the use of barbed sutures for myometrium and subcuticular tissue closure during cesarean deliveries.
